examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Write the recurrence for the returned value separately from the recurrence for work. Trace pre-call actions while descending and post-call actions while unwinding. An activation tree records dynamic calls, not just source-code functions. For nested argument transformations, determine the smallest argument reaching each return-depth threshold.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
f(0)=0 and f(n)=n+f(n−1) for positive integers. Find f(6).

**Answer: 21.** Expansion gives 6+5+4+3+2+1+f(0)=21. Recursion depth is seven activations including the base call, while the numerical result is 21.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Verify that every branch decreases a well-founded measure. A base condition unreachable from the recursive arguments does not guarantee termination.

An exponential number of calls does not imply exponential maximum stack depth.
